MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  MAY 9, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:10 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton

Others Present:  Lou Persichina, Park and Activities Commission
  Victor Yoo, Planning Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The First Grade Daisy Troop No. 3735 led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION

  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PROCLAIMING THE MONTH OF MAY AS "MATERNAL MENTAL
  HEALTH AWARENESS MONTH"

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted her pleasure at presenting Drs. Berkowitz
  and Handler with a Proclamation. She relayed her own experience with
  postpartum depression, and because of family, friends and medical support,
  she was able to overcome this condition.

  Dr. Handler commented that recognition of this mood disorder helps to de-
  stigmatize and manage this illness.

  Dr. Berkowitz further commented that this affects the entire family and is
  thankful for the City’s acknowledgement.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 25,
  2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
MAY 9, 2017
 B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL requested the following addition on Page 6,
  Paragraph 3:

  “COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the Air Quality Management Plan
  was approved by the Air Resources Board.”

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2017 AS
  AMENDED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  JOINT SPECIAL MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION AND
  ADJOURNED MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 1, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE JOINT SPECIAL MEETING OF THE PLANNING
  COMMISSION AND ADJOURNED MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  MINUTES OF MAY 1, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – APRIL AND MAY

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 58348 THROUGH 58379 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $70,651.32; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040117 THROUGH 040217;
  58224 THROUGH 58235; 58268 THROUGH 58287; 58326 THROUGH
  58339 IN THE AMOUNT OF $237,460.92 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $308,112.24 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEM A.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

  APPROVED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 9, 2017
 9.  NEW BUSINESS (Taken out of order)

A.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 1, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MAY 1, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU) BETWEEN THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND THE CALIFORNIA JOINT POWERS INSURANCE
  AUTHORITY (CJPIA) FOR PURPOSES OF AUTHORIZING WORK RELATED TO
  CJPIA'S ADA ASSISTANCE PROGRAM

  Recommendation:  That the City Council approve the Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and the
  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority (CJPIA) for purposes of authorizing
  work related to CJPIA's ADA Assistance Program in the amount of $12,400 for
  the services completed by Disability Access Consultants.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO APPROVE THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU)
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND THE
  CALIFORNIA JOINT POWERS INSURANCE AUTHORITY (CJPIA) FOR
  PURPOSES OF AUTHORIZING WORK RELATED TO CJPIA'S ADA
  ASSISTANCE PROGRAM IN THE AMOUNT OF $12,400 FOR THE
  SERVICES COMPLETED BY DISABILITY ACCESS CONSULTANTS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 33-16; APPLICANT:  MORLEY MENDELSON;
  LOCATION: 4 SILVER SADDLE LANE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Re-open the public hearing; 2)
  Take public testimony; 3) Close the public hearing; 4) Deliberate; and 5)
  Direct staff to prepare a Resolution of Denial or Approval of the Variance
  request.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Senior Planner Naughton noted
  that the Applicant was willing to work with his neighbors who had an issue
  with their view.

  In response to MAYOR ZERUNYAN, Senior Planner Naughton noted that the
  Applicant has agreed to remove the non-conforming carport, but the existing
  fence and gate was shown on the past entitlement plans and were approved at
  that time.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Senior Planner noted that the
  existing hedge provides the visual barrier and will obscure the four foot solar
  panels. Additionally, Planning Director Wahba stated that a condition will be
  included regarding the maintenance of the landscaping which will allow this
  area to be screened to the satisfaction of the City Manager/Planning Director.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 9, 2017
   MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that he has received comments regarding the City
  approving solar panels in the front yard, and it is the COUNCIL’S job to
  determine if the Applicant’s case is a unique circumstance substantially
  different from other residences.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that staff has drafted the variance findings and
  considered this a unique situation since most of the homes in this area are
  built to the rear of the lots, i.e. barbecues, pools, gazebos and would not apply
  as a City-wide decision.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  Morley Mendelson, Applicant, noted that he will respond to any questions the
  COUNCIL may have.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Mendelson noted that he did
  communicate with his neighbors and agreed to trim his trees to reinstate their
  view, but cannot address his other neighbors’ concerns until the COUNCIL
  makes a decision on his project.

  Horace Higgins, 14 Silver Saddle, commented on his support to approve the
  variance as they have a similar situation with their home.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the conditions in the rear would be to
  maintain the hedge to screen the panels and inquired if the property were to be
  sold, would that condition remain. Planning Director Wahba responded that
  the approval runs with the property, not the owner and the future owner would
  still be bound by this approval.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Planning Director Wahba noted
  that if the solar panels were removed, the resolution would be rescinded, but
  the fence would remain due to the location of the pool.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that he would like to thank the Planning
  Commission and staff for all their work because the Commission’s decision
  allowed the COUNCIL to discuss and vote on this unique case. He then
  thanked the Applicant for his cooperation.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL commented that she concurs with staff’s findings
  for the variance. She noted that this case is an exceptional circumstance due
  to the fact that the front yard is actually the rear yard and would allow for solar
  panels to be installed at the requested location. She further noted that this
  approval does not mean any resident can place solar panels in their front yard.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO PREPARE A RESOLUTION OF APPROVAL FOR
  THE VARIANCE REQUESTED INCLUDING CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL
  AND BRING BACK TO THE MAY 23, 2017 MEETING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 9, 2017
 10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 716 - SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES ADDING CHAPTER 9.10 TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO SOCIAL HOST RESPONSIBILITY AND
  LIABILITY FOR HOSTING LOUD OR UNRULY GATHERINGS, INCLUDING
  THOSE WHERE UNDERAGE DRINKING IS OCCURRING AND MAKING OTHER
  CONFORMING CHANGES TO THE MUNICIPAL CODE

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 716.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Ordinance No. 716 by title only.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that she testified in support of the Social
  Host Ordinance at the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors’ hearing.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that  this  ordinance  would  also  affect  the
  unincorporated Peninsula areas.

B.  SALARY SURVEY CITIES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the list of survey cities as
  presented.  After review by the consultant and the Budget and Audit
  Committee, the final salary survey and consultant report will be presented to
  the City Council at the budget workshop.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF requested that the various survey cities’ populations
  be included in the survey.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that he was pleased this survey was
  completed by staff.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE LIST OF SURVEY CITIES AS PRESENTED WITH THE
  FINAL SALARY SURVEY AND CONSULTANT REPORT TO BE
  PRESENTED TO THE CITY COUNCIL AT THE BUDGET WORKSHOP.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 9, 2017
 12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 24, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  APRIL 24, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that good discussion took place regarding
  the Cal Water Project, and they are engaging the equestrian community and
  individual homeowners located along the pipeline project.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN stated that this item should be placed on the website and
  social media. Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that this information will
  be provided to the public.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested sending a thank you letter to Jim Moore
  for his past participation in providing horses for the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride and
  to make sure horses are available next year for the COUNCIL.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that she would like to see the equestrian
  community be more involved.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that the City supports the equestrian
  community, and it would mean a lot to have them involved in City activities.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented on his disappointment at the handful of riders
  who attended the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride. He noted that if the equestrian
  community no longer wishes to participate in this event, perhaps it should be
  eliminated, but would like to see them engaged in this event for next year.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented that if this ride is not of interest, it
  should be eliminated because it takes a good deal of staff time to advertise and
  organize this event.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that there were a number of competing
  events and perhaps they were the reasons the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride was not
  successful. She further noted that the City has a reputation for being an
  equestrian community, and it was her hope to have this event supported.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that if there are other events on the same
  date, then perhaps the day could be changed and coordinate this with the Boy
  Scout Pancake Breakfast.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested that representatives from the Peninsula
  Horsemen’s Association might want to attend an Equestrian Committee
  meeting.

B.  GENERAL PLAN UPDATE

  Planning Director Wahba provided an update on the joint Special Planning
  Commission and Adjourned City Council meeting and background on how the
  General Plan Advisory Committee was created years ago. He noted that he
  provided the COUNCIL with an information letter explaining the duties of the
  Committee, and the general consensus was to go out to the community in an
  effort to determine who would be interested in serving.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MAY 9, 2017
   Planning Director Wahba noted that he will schedule a workshop with the
  consultant in mid-June and invite members of the public for a presentation
  explaining what is involved and the selection process.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that one does not have to be on the
  committee to express an opinion and would encourage participation on a
  specific issue.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that the COUNCIL and staff would be
  involved in the vetting process, and if there are not enough participants, ask the
  Planning Commission for their input.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented on the importance of this issue as it will have a
  long-lasting impact on the City and should be within the COUNCIL’S purview to
  make the appointments.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the final determination should be the
  COUNCIL’S, but it is a good idea to cast a wide net and invite both
  Commissions to make recommendations.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that the consultant would explain the
  process, engage the community and invite those who are interested to fill out an
  application.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN also suggested creating a list of interested parties.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that this item should be mentioned on the
  website.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer also suggested reaching out to the
  homeowners’ associations.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO CONTACT THE CONSULTANT AND SCHEDULE A
  MEETING IN MID-JUNE INVITING MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC AND
  CONSIDER RECOMMENDATIONS BY THE COUNCIL AND STAFF TO
  DETERMINE WHO WILL SERVE ON THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY
  COMMITTEE.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that she attended a COG meeting with Wayne
  Nastri, Executive Director, Air Quality Management District, speaking on
  refinery issues. She noted that Los Angeles County Sheriff McDonnell was
  invited to speak at their next meeting on May 25.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF then announced that there will be a meeting on
  broadband and the municipal fiber network on May 24 from 11:30 a.m. to
  1:00 p.m. She added that the COG is working on the development of Measure M
  Guidelines.

B.  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that Assistant City Manager Grammer and
  Consultant Kathleen McGowan have been working with the offices of Senator
  Allen and Assemblymember Muratsuchi regarding storm water permit
  compliance issues.

C.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that the California Contract Cities Annual Municipal
  Conference is scheduled for the upcoming weekend.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MAY 9, 2017
 14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT: QUARTERLY CITY

  (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957)

  NO ACTION WAS TAKEN.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:58 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Greg Grammer
